title: Brent Crude Tops $100/bbl as Middle East Conflict Escalates
content: Brent crude surged past $100/bbl on 23 July 2026, its highest level since May, after Yemen's Houthi rebels struck Saudi oil tankers in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and a fragile US-Iran ceasefire collapsed, reviving fears of disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. WTI rose in tandem, with Brent up roughly 30% this month. Goldman Sachs warned prices could exceed $120/bbl in Q4 if the blockage persists, with some forecasters seeing Brent averaging near $100 through 2027. The spike rattled global equities, lifted UST and gilt yields, and firmed the USD as investors priced in a fresh inflation shock, complicating the policy path for the Fed, ECB and BoE alike.

title: Fed Rate-Hike Odds Surge as Oil-Driven Inflation Risk Mounts
content: Fed funds futures repriced sharply in the week to 24 July 2026, with markets assigning roughly a one-in-three chance of a hike at the 28-29 July FOMC meeting, up from near-zero a fortnight earlier. Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated that inflation remains 'too high', with PCE running near 3.7-4.1% y/y, well above target, as surging Brent crude adds fresh cost-push pressure. Nine of eighteen FOMC participants now see at least one 2026 hike, a reversal from earlier expectations of cuts. The 10-year UST yield climbed to about 4.70%, its highest since January 2025. A hawkish surprise would pressure EM currencies and risk assets while reinforcing the USD and DXY broadly.

title: Tech-Led Wall Street Selloff as Alphabet, Tesla Spook AI Investors
content: US equities fell sharply on 23 July 2026, with the Nasdaq Composite down 2.15% to 25,137.69 and the Dow off nearly 1%, after Alphabet and Tesla earnings reignited doubts over AI capital spending. Alphabet shares dropped about 7% after lifting 2026 capex guidance to $195-205bn from $180-190bn, while Tesla slid roughly 14-15% on a Q2 earnings miss and negative free cash flow; the two firms shed close to $500bn in combined market value. The selloff compounded pressure from Brent above $100/bbl and rising UST yields. The S&P 500 stabilised near flat on 24 July, though hyperscaler earnings from Amazon, Meta and Microsoft next week are seen as a key test for sentiment.
